page: UpCloud GPU-32xCPU-384GB-3xL4 is an x86_64 architecture server virtualized via KVM. The system features 32 shared vCPUs and 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is provided by three NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace family, delivering a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM.

This configuration does not include local storage, meaning external block storage must be attached for operating system and data storage needs. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is included. A notable hardware tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention under sustained, CPU-heavy workloads compared to dedicated CPU instances.

Given the high memory capacity and triple NVIDIA L4 GPU setup, this server is designed for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning inference, data science pipelines, and parallel processing tasks. The high memory-to-core ratio provides significant resource density for memory-intensive operations, though the shared CPU model suggests it is best optimized for workloads where the primary computational bottleneck is offloaded to the GPU accelerators rather than the host CPU.
